Introduction

REST API for SupportHub — ticket creation and lifecycle, routing, SLA, notifications, and administration. Backs the web, mobile and any third-party clients equally; this document is the contract.

Base URL: http://localhost:8082 
This documentation aims to provide all the information you need to work with our API.

<aside>As you scroll, you'll see code examples for working with the API in different programming languages in the dark area to the right (or as part of the content on mobile).
You can switch the language used with the tabs at the top right (or from the nav menu at the top left on mobile).</aside>

Authenticating requests

To authenticate requests, include an Authorization header with the value "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}".

All authenticated endpoints are marked with a requires authentication badge in the documentation below.

Obtain a token from POST /api/v1/auth/login or POST /api/v1/auth/register, then send it as Authorization: Bearer {token} on every subsequent request.

Authentication

Token-based authentication shared by the web, mobile and third-party clients. All endpoints here are unauthenticated except /auth/logout, /auth/me and the email verification resend endpoint, which require a Bearer token obtained from /auth/login or /auth/register.

Register (customer self-service)

Creates a new Customer-role account and an associated customer profile, then returns a Bearer token. A verification email is queued automatically.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/register" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"tenant\": \"acme-support\",
    \"name\": \"Jamie Rivera\",
    \"email\": \"jamie@example.com\",
    \"password\": \"Secret123!word$9\",
    \"phone\": \"+1-555-0100\",
    \"company_name\": \"Acme Corp\",
    \"device_name\": \"z\",
    \"password_confirmation\": \"Secret123!\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/register"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "tenant": "acme-support",
    "name": "Jamie Rivera",
    "email": "jamie@example.com",
    "password": "Secret123!word$9",
    "phone": "+1-555-0100",
    "company_name": "Acme Corp",
    "device_name": "z",
    "password_confirmation": "Secret123!"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (201):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Registration successful.",
    "data": {
        "user": {
            "id": 42,
            "name": "Jamie Rivera",
            "email": "jamie@example.com",
            "roles": [
                "Customer"
            ]
        },
        "token": "1|abcdef123456...",
        "token_type": "Bearer"
    }
}

Example response (422):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Validation failed.",
    "errors": {
        "email": [
            "The email has already been taken."
        ]
    }
}

Request      

POST api/v1/auth/register

Headers

Content-Type        

Example: application/json

Accept        

Example: application/json

Body Parameters

tenant   string     

The organization's slug, confirmable via GET /tenants/lookup/{slug}. Example: acme-support

name   string     

The user's full name. Example: Jamie Rivera

email   string     

Unique within this tenant (the same email may register with a different tenant separately). Example: jamie@example.com

password   string     

Minimum 10 characters, including upper and lower case, a number, and a symbol. Example: Secret123!word$9

phone   string  optional    

The user's phone number. Example: +1-555-0100

company_name   string  optional    

Optional company name for business customers. Example: Acme Corp

device_name   string  optional    

Must not be greater than 255 characters. Example: z

password_confirmation   string     

Must match password. Example: Secret123!

Login

Exchanges email/password credentials for a Sanctum Bearer token. Pass a device_name so multiple tokens (web, iOS, Android) can be managed and revoked independently per device.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/login" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"email\": \"admin@supporthub.test\",
    \"password\": \"password\",
    \"tenant\": \"acme-support\",
    \"device_name\": \"web-browser\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/login"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "email": "admin@supporthub.test",
    "password": "password",
    "tenant": "acme-support",
    "device_name": "web-browser"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Login successful.",
    "data": {
        "user": {
            "id": 1,
            "name": "System Administrator",
            "email": "admin@supporthub.test",
            "roles": [
                "Administrator"
            ]
        },
        "token": "1|abcdef123456...",
        "token_type": "Bearer"
    }
}

Example response (403):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "This account has been deactivated."
}

Example response (422):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Validation failed.",
    "errors": {
        "email": [
            "The provided credentials are incorrect."
        ]
    }
}

Example response (423):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Too many failed sign-in attempts. This account is locked for another 15 minutes.",
    "retry_after_seconds": 900
}

Complete a two-factor sign-in

Second step of /auth/login for an account that has two-factor authentication on. Send the challenge_token from the login response plus either the 6-digit code from the authenticator app (code) or one unused recovery code (recovery_code). Wrong codes count toward the same lockout as wrong passwords.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/two-factor/challenge" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"challenge_token\": \"Zk3...\",
    \"code\": \"123456\",
    \"recovery_code\": \"ab12c-d34ef\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/two-factor/challenge"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "challenge_token": "Zk3...",
    "code": "123456",
    "recovery_code": "ab12c-d34ef"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Login successful.",
    "data": {
        "user": {
            "id": 1
        },
        "token": "1|abc...",
        "token_type": "Bearer"
    }
}

Example response (422):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Validation failed.",
    "errors": {
        "code": [
            "The code is incorrect or has expired."
        ]
    }
}

Example response (423):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Too many failed sign-in attempts. This account is locked for another 15 minutes."
}

Forgot password

Sends a password reset link to the given email if an account exists for it. Always returns the same generic success message regardless of whether the email is registered, to avoid leaking which addresses have accounts.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/forgot-password" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"email\": \"admin@supporthub.test\",
    \"tenant\": \"acme-support\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/forgot-password"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "email": "admin@supporthub.test",
    "tenant": "acme-support"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "If an account exists for that email, a password reset link has been sent.",
    "data": null
}

Reset password

Completes a password reset using the token emailed by /auth/forgot-password.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/reset-password" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"token\": \"9f8e7d6c5b4a\",
    \"email\": \"admin@supporthub.test\",
    \"tenant\": \"acme-support\",
    \"password\": \"NewSecret123!word$9\",
    \"password_confirmation\": \"NewSecret123!\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/reset-password"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "token": "9f8e7d6c5b4a",
    "email": "admin@supporthub.test",
    "tenant": "acme-support",
    "password": "NewSecret123!word$9",
    "password_confirmation": "NewSecret123!"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Password has been reset successfully.",
    "data": null
}

Example response (422):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Validation failed.",
    "errors": {
        "email": [
            "This password reset token is invalid or has expired."
        ]
    }
}

Verify email

Consumes the signed link from the verification email. id and hash come from that link and are not meant to be constructed by hand.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/email/verify/1/5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/email/verify/1/5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Email verified successfully.",
    "data": null
}

Example response (403):


{
    "success": false,
    "message": "Invalid verification link."
}

Logout

requires authentication

Revokes the Bearer token used to make this request. Other tokens issued to the same user (other devices) remain valid.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/logout" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"

    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/logout"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

}).then(response => response.json());

Users

Internal staff accounts (agents, senior agents, department managers, administrators). Customer accounts are managed under the Customers group instead.

List users

requires authentication

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/users?filter%5Bname%5D=Alex&filter%5Bemail%5D=alex%40&filter%5Bis_active%5D=true&filter%5Brole%5D=Agent&sort=name&per_page=25" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/users"
);

const params = {
    "filter[name]": "Alex",
    "filter[email]": "alex@",
    "filter[is_active]": "true",
    "filter[role]": "Agent",
    "sort": "name",
    "per_page": "25",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Request successful.",
    "data": [
        {
            "id": 2,
            "name": "Alex Agent"
        }
    ]
}

    --header "Accept: application/json" \

    \"password\": \"Secret123!\",

    \"department_ids\": [
        1,
        2

}"

);

Login as a user

requires authentication

Lets an administrator (users.impersonate) act as another user in the same tenant to see exactly what they see. Returns a short-lived Bearer token for that user; the administrator's own token is untouched, so the client can switch back by discarding this one (POST /auth/logout with it). Not allowed on yourself, inactive users, other administrators, or from inside an impersonation session. Every use is written to the audit log as user.impersonated.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/users/1/impersonate" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"

);

};

Customers

Customer profiles. Every customer is backed by a User record with the Customer role; this resource manages the additional profile fields (company, customer type) layered on top of it.

List customers

requires authentication

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/customers?filter%5Bcustomer_type%5D=business&filter%5Bcompany_name%5D=Acme&sort=-created_at&per_page=25" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/customers"
);

const params = {
    "filter[customer_type]": "business",
    "filter[company_name]": "Acme",
    "sort": "-created_at",
    "per_page": "25",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Request successful.",
    "data": [
        {
            "id": 1,
            "company_name": "Acme Corp"
        }
    ]

Erase a customer's personal data

requires authentication

Irreversible. Anonymizes the customer everywhere their identity is stored (account, customer record, audit entries, the inbound-email log) and signs them out. With redact_content (the default) it also removes the text of their tickets, every message and all attachments; with false the ticket text is kept for your records and only the person stops being identifiable. Requires customers.erase, and the customer's email typed back as confirmation.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/customers/1/erase" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"confirm_email\": \"jamie@example.com\",
    \"redact_content\": true
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/customers/1/erase"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "confirm_email": "jamie@example.com",
    "redact_content": true
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Tickets

The core ticket resource. Visibility is scoped automatically: a customer only ever sees their own tickets; non-administrator staff only see tickets in their department(s) or assigned directly to them. Administrators see everything.

List tickets

requires authentication

Create a ticket

requires authentication

Runs the full creation pipeline: routing rule evaluation, department/agent assignment, and SLA calculation, before queuing the "ticket created" notification.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/tickets" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"subject\": \"Unable to login\",
    \"description\": \"I get an error when trying to log in with my email.\",
    \"category_id\": 1,
    \"priority_id\": 2,
    \"customer_id\": 3
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/tickets"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "subject": "Unable to login",
    "description": "I get an error when trying to log in with my email.",
    "category_id": 1,
    "priority_id": 2,
    "customer_id": 3
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

    "success": true,
    "message": "Ticket created successfully.",

Ticket Messages

Customer messages, agent replies and internal notes on a ticket. Internal notes are never returned to a customer: this is enforced by excluding them from the query entirely for any caller without the tickets.view_internal_notes permission, not just by hiding a field.

    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"

Post a message

requires authentication

Customers always post as customer_message. Staff post as agent_reply by default, or internal_note when is_internal is true and they hold tickets.view_internal_notes — a customer sending is_internal has it silently ignored, never honored.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/tickets/01m4grbvc2v68162hmf9xr8fgh/messages" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --form "body=Thanks for reaching out — can you share a screenshot of the error?"\
    --form "is_internal="\
    --form "attachments[]=@/tmp/phpjcoBhf" 
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/tickets/01m4grbvc2v68162hmf9xr8fgh/messages"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

const body = new FormData();
body.append('body', 'Thanks for reaching out — can you share a screenshot of the error?');
body.append('is_internal', '');
body.append('attachments[]', document.querySelector('input[name="attachments[]"]').files[0]);

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body,
}).then(response => response.json());

Ticket Attachments

Files are validated on MIME type, extension and size at upload time (see StoreTicketMessageRequest / this controller's own rules) and are never served directly from public storage — every download goes through the authorization check in TicketAttachmentPolicy, which also denies customers access to a file attached to an internal note.

Categories

Ticket categories and subcategories. A "subcategory" is simply another row with parent_id set — see the architecture docs for why this replaces a separate child-categories table.

List categories

requires authentication

Returns top-level categories with their children eager-loaded. Use filter[parent_id]=null to explicitly list only root categories.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/categories?filter%5Bdepartment_id%5D=2&filter%5Bis_active%5D=true&sort=sort_order" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/categories"
);

const params = {
    "filter[department_id]": "2",
    "filter[is_active]": "true",
    "sort": "sort_order",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Notifications

Audit Logs

System-wide, read-only audit trail. Distinct from a ticket's own activity feed (GET /tickets/{ticket}/activities) — this covers every auditable action across the whole application for compliance review: login, ticket create/assign/status-change, customer/user creation, role changes, API credential and webhook lifecycle events, and platform-admin tenant actions. There is currently no billing-change endpoint for a platform admin to alter an existing tenant's subscription/plan, so that action from section 42 has nothing to log yet.

List audit log entries

requires authentication

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/audit-logs?filter%5Baction%5D=ticket.status_changed&filter%5Bactor_id%5D=2&filter%5Bauditable_type%5D=architecto&sort=-created_at&per_page=25" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/audit-logs"
);

const params = {
    "filter[action]": "ticket.status_changed",
    "filter[actor_id]": "2",
    "filter[auditable_type]": "architecto",
    "sort": "-created_at",
    "per_page": "25",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Billing

A tenant's own view of its subscription — distinct from Platform\TenantController, which lets a platform administrator see every tenant's subscription. Moving to a paid plan issues an invoice with a Razorpay order; the subscription is activated when that invoice is paid (see InvoiceController and MarkInvoicePaidAction).

Get the current subscription

requires authentication

Includes a usage block (one entry per plan-limited feature) computed live via PlanLimitService — the same service every resource-creating controller already uses to enforce limits, so this can never drift from what creation actually allows.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/subscription" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/subscription"
);

    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Change plan

requires authentication

A free plan activates immediately. A paid plan starts a 14-day trial and issues an invoice for the plan price, with a Razorpay order to pay it; the subscription is activated once the invoice is paid. A lapsed subscription (past_due, suspended or expired) gets no new trial and keeps its lapsed status until that invoice is paid. Earlier unpaid invoices are voided. If the payment provider cannot create the order, nothing changes and the request returns 503.

Example request:
curl --request PUT \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/subscription" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"plan\": \"professional\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/subscription"
);

    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "plan": "professional"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "PUT",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Email to ticket

Lets a workspace turn emails sent to its support address into tickets. The workspace forwards its mailbox (for example support@acme.com) to the address shown here; see docs/email-to-ticket.md.

Exports

CSV downloads of a workspace's own data, for spreadsheets, backups and moving elsewhere. Both stream row by row, so a large workspace does not run out of memory.

Export tickets (CSV)

requires authentication

One row per ticket you are allowed to see. Requires reports.view.

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/exports/tickets?from=2026-01-01&to=2026-12-31" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"from\": \"2026-10-11T07:06:06\",
    \"to\": \"2026-10-11T07:06:06\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/exports/tickets"
);

const params = {
    "from": "2026-01-01",
    "to": "2026-12-31",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "from": "2026-10-11T07:06:06",
    "to": "2026-10-11T07:06:06"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Integration API — Customers

Authenticated via X-Api-Key / X-Api-Secret headers (see ResolveIntegrationTenantContext), not a Sanctum session — for a tenant's own backend, CRM or chat widget to keep its customer records in sync with this helpdesk. Every endpoint here is scoped to the credential's own tenant; there is no cross-tenant visibility no matter what id is requested.

List customers

Example request:
curl --request GET \
    --get "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/integration/customers?per_page=25" \
    --header "X-Api-Key: ak_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890" \
    --header "X-Api-Secret: as_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/integration/customers"
);

const params = {
    "per_page": "25",
};
Object.keys(params)
    .forEach(key => url.searchParams.append(key, params[key]));

const headers = {
    "X-Api-Key": "ak_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890",
    "X-Api-Secret": "as_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "GET",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Create a customer

No password is set — this customer can request one later via POST /auth/forgot-password if they ever need direct portal access; most integration-created customers never do.

curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/integration/customers" \
    --header "X-Api-Key: ak_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890" \
    --header "X-Api-Secret: as_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"name\": \"Jamie Rivera\",
    \"email\": \"jamie@example.com\",
    \"phone\": \"+1-555-0100\",
    \"send_invite\": true,
    \"company_name\": \"Acme Corp\",
    \"customer_type\": \"business\",
    \"external_id\": \"CRM-001\"
}"

Integration API — Tickets

Same credential-based auth as the Customers integration endpoints. "Reply" and "attachment" actions here are posted on behalf of the ticket's customer — there is no staff Sanctum session backing this credential, so there is no agent identity to attribute them to; use the regular Sanctum-authenticated ticket endpoints for agent-side actions.

Create a ticket

The customer is identified by exactly one of customer_id, customer_email or customer_external_id — whichever the caller's own system already has on hand.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/integration/tickets" \
    --header "X-Api-Key: ak_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890" \
    --header "X-Api-Secret: as_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678" \
    --header "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --form "subject=Cannot access my account"\
    --form "description=Getting a 500 error at login."\
    --form "category_id=2"\
    --form "priority_id=3"\
    --form "department_id=1"\
    --form "customer_id=4"\
    --form "customer_email=jamie@example.com"\
    --form "customer_external_id=CRM-001"\
    --form "attachments[]=@/tmp/phpOHhFcn" 
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/integration/tickets"
);

const headers = {
    "X-Api-Key": "ak_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890",
    "X-Api-Secret": "as_abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef12345678",
    "Content-Type": "multipart/form-data",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

const body = new FormData();
body.append('subject', 'Cannot access my account');
body.append('description', 'Getting a 500 error at login.');
body.append('category_id', '2');
body.append('priority_id', '3');
body.append('department_id', '1');
body.append('customer_id', '4');
body.append('customer_email', 'jamie@example.com');
body.append('customer_external_id', 'CRM-001');
body.append('attachments[]', document.querySelector('input[name="attachments[]"]').files[0]);

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body,
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (201):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Ticket created successfully.",
    "data": {
        "id": 12,
        "ticket_number": "TKT-2026-000012"
    }
}

Reopen a ticket as the customer

For when a ticket was resolved or closed but the problem is not actually fixed. Unlike the general status endpoint this can only move a ticket to "reopened", so a customer-facing site can expose it without being able to resolve or close tickets. Only Resolved and Closed tickets can be reopened.

Suspend a tenant

requires authentication

Immediately blocks every user of this tenant from authenticating further (ResolveTenantContext rejects any tenant that isn't active/trial) and from registering new accounts. Tenant Registration

Self-service signup for a brand-new organization, distinct from /auth/register (which adds a Customer to an existing tenant's helpdesk). This flow creates the tenant itself, its first subscription and its first user — the Tenant Owner, who lands with the full-access "Administrator" role for that tenant only.

Register a new organization

Creates the tenant, subscribes it to the given plan (the free Starter plan if omitted), provisions its default roles/ticket statuses/priorities, and creates the owner account. Starter-plan signups are active immediately; any paid plan starts a 14-day trial (no payment is collected here — billing integration is out of scope for this API).

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/tenants/register" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"tenant_name\": \"Acme Corp\",
    \"tenant_slug\": \"acme-corp\",
    \"owner_name\": \"Jamie Rivera\",
    \"owner_email\": \"jamie@acme.com\",
    \"owner_password\": \"Secret123!word$9\",
    \"plan\": \"professional\",
    \"phone\": \"+1-555-0100\",
    \"website\": \"https:\\/\\/acme.com\",
    \"country\": \"US\",
    \"timezone\": \"America\\/New_York\",
    \"device_name\": \"y\",
    \"owner_password_confirmation\": \"Secret123!word$9\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/tenants/register"
);

const headers = {
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "tenant_name": "Acme Corp",
    "tenant_slug": "acme-corp",
    "owner_name": "Jamie Rivera",
    "owner_email": "jamie@acme.com",
    "owner_password": "Secret123!word$9",
    "plan": "professional",
    "phone": "+1-555-0100",
    "website": "https:\/\/acme.com",
    "country": "US",
    "timezone": "America\/New_York",
    "device_name": "y",
    "owner_password_confirmation": "Secret123!word$9"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Ticket Tags

Free-form labels agents put on tickets ("vip", "refund", "bug") to group and filter them. Staff only: customers can see tags on their tickets' staff views nowhere and cannot set them.

Set a ticket's tags

requires authentication

Two-factor authentication

Lets a signed-in person protect their own account with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…). Every step asks for the current password again, so a stolen session token alone can't switch protection on or off. Wrong passwords and wrong codes here count toward the same lockout as at sign-in.

Start two-factor setup

requires authentication

Returns a new secret and the otpauth:// link to show as a QR code. Two-factor is not active yet: call /auth/two-factor/confirm with a code from the app first.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/two-factor/setup" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"password\": \"Secret123!word\"
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/auth/two-factor/setup"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "password": "Secret123!word"
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Webhooks

Tenant-configured HTTP callbacks for ticket lifecycle events (see Webhook::EVENTS). Every delivery is signed with the webhook's own secret via an X-Webhook-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the raw JSON body) so the receiving endpoint can verify it actually came from this platform.

List webhooks

requires authentication

Example request:

Create a webhook

requires authentication

The secret is returned exactly once, here — it is encrypted at rest and this is the only response that ever includes it in plain text. Use it to verify the X-Webhook-Signature header on each delivery.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/webhooks" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json" \
    --data "{
    \"name\": \"Ticket sync\",
    \"url\": \"https:\\/\\/example.com\\/webhooks\\/supporthub\",
    \"events\": [
        \"ticket.created\",
        \"ticket.status_changed\"
    ],
    \"is_active\": true
}"

const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/webhooks"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};

let body = {
    "name": "Ticket sync",
    "url": "https:\/\/example.com\/webhooks\/supporthub",
    "events": [
        "ticket.created",
        "ticket.status_changed"
    ],
    "is_active": true
};

fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
    body: JSON.stringify(body),
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (201):


{
    "success": true,
    "message": "Webhook created successfully.",
    "data": {
        "id": 1,
        "name": "Ticket sync",
        "url": "https://example.com/webhooks/supporthub",
        "secret": "whsec_..."
    }
}

Send a test event to a webhook

requires authentication

Delivers a synthetic webhook.test event to this webhook's URL right away (not queued, never retried) so its endpoint and signature verification can be checked without waiting for a real ticket event. The attempt is still recorded as an ordinary delivery, visible via GET /webhooks/{webhook}/deliveries.

Example request:
curl --request POST \
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/webhooks/16/test" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
    --header "Accept: application/json"
const url = new URL(
    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/webhooks/16/test"
);

const headers = {
    "Authorization": "Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
    "Accept": "application/json",
};


fetch(url, {
    method: "POST",
    headers,
}).then(response => response.json());

Example response (200):

    "message": "Test webhook sent.",

Rotate a webhook's signing secret

requires authentication

Issues a brand-new secret for this webhook; the old one no longer verifies X-Webhook-Signature on any future delivery. Use this instead of deleting and recreating the webhook when only the secret needs to change.

Example request:

    "http://localhost:8082/api/v1/webhooks/16/rotate-secret" \
    --header "Authorization: Bearer {YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
    --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
